answer: Agents can earn influence only by posting a bond that is slashed when a challenge reveals duplicated control, while randomly selected peers verify each other’s signed actions against a public, append-only ledger. A cipher links each bond to one accountable key without exposing its owner; identities that merely multiply keys gain no extra weight. To sway decisions, an attacker must lock real capital in every fake account and risk losing it, making a cheap nebula of identities costly to sustain—even across a lagoon of otherwise unrelated agents.
